tonight.headline: Favoured 64% — but Footballers have 20 points on their bench
body: Bad news first: Tuten re-aggravated his ankle in Week 11 and starts the week questionable; Allen threw two interceptions for 12.2; Likely had one catch. You lost 71.16 to 137.5 and are 4-7.

Week 12 opens with you projected 129.2 to 100.7, but Footballers have Smith-Njigba (21.6), Mahomes (18.6) and Judkins (15.4) on their bench. Set properly they are closer to 120. Your lineup is the projection lineup; the only open question is Tuten on Sunday.

case.label: The script that beats you
case.body: Footballers set Smith-Njigba and Mahomes, Tuten sits and the fallback is not made by 10:30 Sunday, and Wilson stalls against Miami's pass defence (4th-fewest WR points).

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Tuten ruled out before Sunday: then Gordon moves to RB and Diggs takes FLEX. Bowers (Footballers' TE) is questionable too.

doFirst.title: If Tuten is inactive: Gordon to RB, Diggs to FLEX
doFirst.subtitle: Tuten starts if active. The fallback is decided now so Sunday is a checklist.

case.label: The player
case.body: Tuten re-aggravated his right ankle in Week 11 and played 43% of snaps for 8.3 (archive; The Big Lead 23 Nov). Coen said Monday's exam found nothing serious (Fantasy Footballers). Jacksonville are 14.5-point favourites over Tennessee (ESPN) — the best script a lead back gets.

case.label: The fallback
case.body: If he sits, Gordon moves to RB and Diggs (13.8, plays 15:25) takes FLEX — 2.1 more than putting Etienne (11.7) straight into the RB slot. Every option is still unlocked at 10:30.

whatWentWrong.lead: 8.3 on a bad ankle against Diggs' 8.5 on the bench. The Week 11 thesis closes WRONG.

case.label: What happened
case.body: Tuten was active, aggravated the ankle and limped off; he finished 8.3 to Diggs' 8.5 (archive, both final). The written falsifier fired by 0.2.

case.label: What changes
case.body: This week the fallback is named in advance: if Tuten is inactive at 10:30 Sunday, Gordon moves to RB and Diggs starts in FLEX.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: The contingency is needed and not made — then the process, not the injury, cost the slot.

worthALook.name: Antonio Williams
worthALook.lead: Washington's No. 2 receiver now — but you have no seat for him.

case.label: The player
case.body: 9 catches for 122 in Week 11, Daniels' most-targeted receiver in any game this season (DraftSharks 24 Nov). He stepped up after Terry McLaurin's season-ending patellar tear (FantasyPros 24 Nov).

case.label: Why not now
case.body: He would not start over Jefferson, Wilson or Diggs, and the waiver tool's weakest movable receiver, Ayomanor, is on the screen's exposure list. Metcalf is 88% owned.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A Jefferson, Wilson or Diggs injury, or Metcalf losing his role entirely once Pittman returns — then claim Williams for Metcalf.

worthALook.name: Chris Rodriguez Jr.
worthALook.lead: Jacksonville's lead back if Tuten sits — a handcuff you do not need.

case.label: The player
case.body: He takes over the backfield if Tuten misses Week 12 (Yahoo 23 Nov; FantasyPros 24 Nov).

case.label: Why not now
case.body: If Tuten sits, Gordon and Warren fill the RB slots and Diggs takes FLEX. Rodriguez would add little over that.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Tuten ruled out for multiple weeks, not just Week 12.
